liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **When Push Comes To Shove** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it the best version of this song they have heard; Reviewer counts it among the weaker songs of the night [18][22]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Weir's microphone was off for part of the first verse [12]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Reviewer finds this version lacking the bite of the best ones [12]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Described as a barnburner [13]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Jerry's singing of the 'wish I was a headlight' line is singled out [13]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): An attendee still remembers the Dew vividly [18]
- **Black Muddy River** (1 review): Reviewer counts it among the weaker songs; Jerry later dropped it after a few tours [22]
- Jerry's guitar work is crisp, inventive and authoritative [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd87-05-02 t01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-05-02 t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-05-02 t03 West LA Fadeaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-05-02 t04 Beat It On Down The Line**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-05-02 t05 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-05-02 t06 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-05-02 t07 Dire Wolf**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-05-02 t08 Far From Me**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-05-02.141909.ultramatrix.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 157 min [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is heavy on ambient mics, with PA and mix issues during Hell In A Bucket [1]
- **gd1987-05-02.166935.Frost.PaloAltoCA.Ultramatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1648**: soundboard; 21 songs; 156 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1987-05-02.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83737.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 152 min; rated 3.86/5 by 14 [4]
- **gd1987-05-02.166841.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 21 songs; 156 min [5]
- **gd1987-05-02.schoeps.grace.gems.105509.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 158 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: The Schoeps recording has an echoing sound during Morning Dew [22]
- **gd1987-05-02.148780.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 146 min [7]

## Around the show

- A slightly windy afternoon put wind noise in audience tapes; the center-field bathroom flooded [18]
- An attendee saw Jerry's limo leaving campus along Palm Drive and shouted thanks to him [19]
- The afternoon felt like the old free park shows or a university amphitheatre Sunday [19]
- Little Red Rooster is decent but has been played too often on this tour [12]
- Reviewer ranks this and Worcester as the best '87 shows they have heard [13]
- Early '87 band shows controlled, marshalled energy, producing some of the decade's best jamming [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-05-02.141909.ultramatrix.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master UltraMatrix PCM > PCM [1]
- **gd1987-05-02.166935.Frost.PaloAltoCA.Ultramatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1648**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 29, 2024; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R) [2]. Also: Derived from the 166841 2496 version, converted down to 16-bit/48 kHz-style 1648 [2]
- **gd1987-05-02.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83737.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Maxell MX90/Sony D5) [4]. Also: The show was broadcast on KZSU; the reviewer's off-air tapes sounded poor [19]
- **gd1987-05-02.166841.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 29, 2024; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R) [5]
- **gd1987-05-02.schoeps.grace.gems.105509.flac16**: taped by Michael Grace; transferred by Michael Grace and Jamie Waddell and Patrick White; source: Schoeps CMC-32s (Omni) spaced 10 foot, 0 degrees > Grace 18V mic power supply, polypropylene coupling capacitors > PCM-F1/SL-2000 Betamax Sony SL-HF900 [6]
- **gd1987-05-02.148780.neumann.km84i.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; Neumann KM84i mics > Sony D5M [7]. Also: A Schoeps CMC32 source patches a 0:07 gap in the Dire Wolf to Far From Me transition; The same Schoeps source supplies a 0:52 patch in Drums [7]
